title: Summer hours
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The college is out. Monday has nothing in it. Wood drives to Newport anyway and sits in Lot C, which is empty, and draws the empty lot, which he did in October. He compares them. The line is different. The lot isn't.

panels.composition: Lot C, empty, May, the pollen gone, the lines bright. The Datsun in its spot.

image.prompt: an empty college parking lot in late spring with bright painted lines and a single small car in its usual spot, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the lot. Beside it, the October drawing from the back of the pad, folded out. Two lots.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a fresh ink drawing of an empty lot beside an older folded-out drawing of the same lot, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD looking from one to the other. BARNABY on the box. The line: October's nervous, May's not. The lot the same.

image.prompt: a young man comparing two drawings of a parking lot while a small dog rests on a box behind him, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The car in the lot. Nobody. The guard's post empty for summer too. The strip has a place now and it's a parking lot in a town that isn't his.

image.prompt: a small car alone in an empty college parking lot with an empty guard's post nearby, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: October's line and May's. The lot is the same; the hand isn't.
